name: Erik Weber

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government, and your answers are confidential. What does your factory work involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I run a router that cuts cabinet panels from boards. I load the board, check the jig and measure the first slot before the panels go to assembly. I came in after delivery work and am a junior operator at 58, still learning how the wood behaves under a fresh bit. I finished secondary school and my wage is about ordinary for this job.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home like, and how do you use new tools?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Clara works a pharmacy counter, and our grown children live nearby but support their own homes. We have a mortgage and just under four months of expenses saved. A few other wood-products plants are within a reasonable trip, if they have actual openings. I ask an AI tool almost every day to explain a router code or sketch a checklist, but I check every dimension against the drawing and ask the setter before changing a bit. I like trying things early, as long as the guard stays on and someone knows how to stop the machine. We would like to ease out of shifts later, but have not priced that yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the cabinet crew that faster office plans do not make a board square. We still have to measure the first routed slot and keep the bit guarded.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our two pay packets cover the mortgage and nearly four months saved is a useful cushion. I am new to routing and need work time to get good at it. This quiet picture gives me that time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep measuring the first panel against the drawing and ask the setter before altering the jig. I would use AI to organise my shift questions, then check the numbers on paper.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm enough. I can learn the machine in stages without my hours changing suddenly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is your first check on a panel?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I put the gauge into the first slot before the next board is fed. A cabinet panel can look straight and still leave a hinge sitting crooked. The setter taught me to measure before admiring the finish.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you run an AI-generated router programme?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not directly. I ask the tool what a code means, then compare the programme with the approved drawing and the setter’s instructions. A clever sentence does not measure a slot.

say: I would **keep** measuring routed slots after office plans get faster.
The **jig** and guard still need checks at the machine.
think: Our **two** wages cover the mortgage and nearly four months saved gives breathing room.
I **need** practice as a junior router operator.
do: **Keep** checking first cabinet panels with the gauge and setter.
**Use** AI for shift questions while verifying dimensions against approved drawings.
feel: **Calm** about continued work and time to improve machine skill.
S0.quote: A cabinet panel can look straight and still leave a hinge sitting crooked.
fieldNote: **Erik** is a junior cabinet-panel router operator, learning jigs and wood behaviour after delivery work.
He **uses** AI daily for code explanations but verifies every dimension with a drawing and experienced setter.
His **ordinary** wage and wife Clara’s pharmacy work cover the mortgage, with just under four months saved.

steps.text: Keep gauging first cabinet panels and checking settings with setter

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew that planning software may change orders before a robot begins loading boards and changing bits. I would ask for a proper guarded test rather than an impressive minute on a screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A loader could eventually let fewer operators cover the router. I am still junior, so I would be easy to leave off a shift. Nearly four months saved helps, but it cannot replace my ordinary wage for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would request a full safe loader trial and compare damaged panels with our present scrap book. If the plant offers paid instruction on its new AI inspection display, I would learn the screen and check its rejection marks against physical measurements. If a router-checking job is posted locally, I would apply only if net pay after travel and its hours cover our mortgage and Clara’s shift pattern.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the roster, yet interested in a useful display. I would learn a screen sooner than a robot arm, because the arm needs supervised isolation practice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you touch the loader during the test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. First I would watch the guard stops and ask a fitter how to lock out the arm. I would take an offered funded paid supervised place to practise controls, not touch them because I watched a trial. The trial tells me what to ask.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no checking job opens?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the router wage and check posted machine jobs at nearby wood plants. The vacancy, pay after travel and shift have to be real and workable before I apply. Our grown children cannot be my fallback pay packet.

say: I would **ask** for a full guarded trial before robot board loading.
I would **learn** a new AI inspection display only on paid instruction.
think: A **later** loader could cut junior router shifts.
**Nearly** four months saved cannot carry a long wage gap.
do: **Request** guarded loader trial and compare panel scrap.
**Learn** offered AI inspection screen on paid time against physical measurements.
**Apply** for posted local router-checking work only with mortgage-covering net pay and hours.
feel: **Anxious** about shifts, curious about a proved inspection screen.
S1.quote: I would learn a screen sooner than a robot arm, because the arm needs supervised isolation practice.
fieldNote: **Erik** separates observing a robot trial from operating it; controls need an offered funded paid supervised place.
He would **actually** learn a new AI inspection display through paid instruction and physical cross-checks.
**Checking** and fallback jobs each need postings, viable pay after travel and workable shifts.

steps.text: Request full guarded loader trial and compare damaged panels
Learn offered AI inspection display on paid time with physical checks
Apply for posted router-checking job only with mortgage-covering net pay after travel and hours
Check posted wood-machine jobs if no checking role and net pay and shift fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my family that AGI can redraw office plans in 2028, while capable robots moving boards, changing bits and checking panels around 2031 threaten the machine shifts. We need actual job terms before the second date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the router crew to shrink sharply once robots can tend a complete board run. I will be 63 then. We have almost four months saved and Clara has her own wage, but the mortgage would still be hard if my pay vanished for months; I would lose sleep doing the sums.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Clara and I would defer replacing the old car and put the mortgage, heating and food amounts on paper. I would ask the factory for written retraining and severance terms. I would apply for a posted local quality-checking role only if it includes paid supervised machine-safety training and net pay after travel and hours that meet our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about losing the router wage. I can try a new tool quickly, but I cannot teach myself a paid job into existence.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you move straight into robot maintenance?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not from a router checklist. I need a real funded paid course with a fitter who can show and test lockout. My willingness to learn does not make the robot arm safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your children for mortgage help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have their own places and costs. I might ask them to read a job posting with me, but I would not write their money into our budget. Clara and I need work and figures we can count.

say: I would **separate** 2028 office AGI from hands-on robots around 2031.
I would **ask** for written jobs and training terms.
think: **Almost** four months saved and a second wage may not protect the mortgage for long.
do: **Delay** car replacement and list essential bills.
**Ask** factory for written retraining and severance terms.
**Apply** for posted quality work only with paid safe instruction and bill-covering net pay and hours.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected wage loss and sleepless mortgage calculations.
S2.quote: I feel alarmed about losing the router wage.
fieldNote: **Erik** expects capable robots to cut router work around 2031, after 2028 AGI changes planning.
His **adaptable** habits do not solve the wage risk; he expects a sharp cut and loses sleep over the mortgage.
A **quality-job** application needs a real posting, paid supervised safety instruction and sufficient net pay after travel.

steps.text: Defer planned car replacement and list mortgage heating and food bills
Ask factory for written retraining and severance terms
Apply for posted quality work with paid safety training bill-covering net pay after travel and shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues that five years ought to buy proper paid robot instruction for newer operators too. AGI changes plans in 2031 and capable machines tend the router around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 66 by that robot date. I have learned to use AI daily, but it does not show me how to isolate a moving arm. We might be able to retire later, yet the mortgage makes it wrong to assume we can stop at 66.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would enrol in an offered recognised automation-inspection course only if it is funded, pays my class hours and includes supervised guard and lockout practice at a time I can attend. After qualifying I would apply for a posted local inspection job only if net pay after travel and shifts cover the mortgage. Without a paid place I would keep the router shift and look at posted nearby machine jobs with enough pay and workable hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about whether the course and job will be real. I would enjoy learning the controls if a trainer is there and my pay continues.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would an online course help you start?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: For a diagram, yes; I would use AI to make questions for the trainer. But I need the fitter beside me while I stop and prove the arm cannot restart. I would never treat a video as proof I can isolate the robot arm.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why not retire when the robots arrive?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Clara and I have not added up actual retirement income against the mortgage and living costs. I would request written estimates before setting a date. If they fall short, I need a paid job.

say: I would **ask** for funded paid practical instruction for junior operators.
2031 **planning** changes precede capable router robots around 2034.
think: At 66, **daily** AI use does not establish robot safety skill.
Our **mortgage** makes retirement conditional on actual income.
do: **Enrol** in offered recognised funded paid course with supervised lockout and attendable hours.
**Apply** after qualification for posted inspection job only with mortgage-covering net pay after travel and shifts.
If **no** paid place, seek posted nearby machine work with sufficient pay and hours.
feel: **Anxious** about places and jobs, interested in supervised new controls.
S3.quote: I would never treat a video as proof I can isolate the robot arm.
fieldNote: **Erik** would enrol only in an offered recognised funded paid course with supervised guard and isolation practice.
**After** qualifying he separately applies for a posted inspection role at net pay after travel that covers the mortgage.
**Without** a paid place he keeps the router wage and checks viable posted local machine jobs.

steps.text: Enrol in offered funded paid recognised course with supervised lockout and attendable hours
Apply after qualification for posted inspection job only with mortgage-covering net pay after travel and shifts
Seek posted machine jobs if no paid course and pay and hours suffice

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my sons that ten years is long enough to learn safely and count what retirement really costs. AGI changes plans in 2036 and capable hands-on robots tend the router around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 68 in 2036 and 71 by the robot date. We might have stopped full shifts, but our mortgage and the rest of the bills decide that, not the date on a card. If I still need factory work, I need an actual paid route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would get written retirement-income and cost estimates this year. If we still need my wage, I would take an offered recognised funded paid course with supervised robot isolation on workable hours, then apply for a posted local inspection job only if net pay after travel and shifts meet our bills. Without that paid course, I would seek posted machine work at adequate wages and hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about money so far ahead, but the long warning lets us make choices. The factory would still have to offer the training and job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you teach younger operators the AI checklist?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I already show another operator how to compare an AI explanation with the approved drawing. I would keep doing that while I have a router shift. I would not ask anyone to trust a chatbot with a guard setting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you decide when to stop working?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Clara and I would compare the written retirement income with mortgage, food and health costs. If the figures cover them, we might choose to leave full shifts. If they do not, we will search for safe paid work, not assume an age fixes it.

say: I would **ask** for real retirement figures and a safe paid route.
2036 **plan** changes come before physical router robots around 2039.
think: At 68 in 2036 I **may** have left paid shifts if income permits.
At 71 **near** 2039 any factory work depends on household costs.
do: **Request** written retirement income and cost figures.
If **wages** are needed, take offered funded paid supervised course on workable hours.
**After** qualification, apply for posted inspection work only with bill-covering net pay and shifts.
feel: **Uneasy** about uncertain retirement income, willing to use the long warning.
S4.quote: I would not ask anyone to trust a chatbot with a guard setting.
fieldNote: **Erik** makes no assumption about retirement payments or working at 71; written figures govern the choice.
If **wages** are needed, course enrolment requires an offered recognised funded paid place with safe practice and workable hours.
An **inspection** application needs a posted job and viable net pay after travel; without training he checks other machine work.

Apply after course for posted inspection job only with bill-covering net pay after travel and shifts

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The two-year picture worries me most because capable robots could cut router shifts around 2031 while Clara and I still pay the mortgage. An offered paid safety course and a posted job with enough net pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I did not ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: I use AI every day and I will show a co-worker how to check its numbers. A cabinet panel can look straight and still leave a hinge sitting crooked.

headlineQuote: I use AI every day and I will show a co-worker how to check its numbers.
portrait: **Erik** Weber, 58, is a junior cabinet-panel router operator with secondary schooling and typical machine pay.
He and **pharmacy-counter** worker wife Clara have grown sons, a mortgage and just under four months saved.
He **uses** AI daily for codes and checklists but verifies dimensions and safety with drawings and a setter.
**Curious** about tools and practical teaching, he still expects robot cuts to threaten his paid shifts.
**Retirement** depends on actual income figures; training and any job need offered paid safe places and viable posted wages.
biggestWorry: **Capable** robots around 2031 could cut his junior router shifts while mortgage payments remain.
whatWouldHelp: **Offer** recognised funded paid robot safety instruction and posted jobs with sufficient net wages and workable shifts.
